Though this appeal is listed for
Admission, with the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the same is taken up for final
disposal.

2. This appeal is filed by the injured claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded
under the judgment and award dated 12.07.2022 passed in M.V.C. No.2777/2017 by the Xi
Additional District Judge & Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi (for short, 'the
Tribunal').
3.

entities.text: Additional District Judge & Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case leading to filing of this appeal are that on 09.10.2017, the appellant/claimant was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing registration No.MH- 10/BJ-9921 at a moderate speed, and at that time, a Truck bearing registration No.MH-10/A-6488 driven by its driver NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the motorcycle of the appellant/claimant due to which he fell down and the front wheel of truck ran over his left leg and thereby sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, he filed a claim petition seeking compensation.
Notices were issued to owner and insurer of the truck.
Respondent No.1-owner of the truck though served with the notice, remained absent and was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2-insurer of the truck appeared and contested the claim petition.

The Tribunal recorded the evidence and on the basis of the evidence placed before it, awarded total compensation of Rs.31,57,693/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.

4. Sri. Umesh C.Ainapur, learned counsel for the appellant, submits that the Tribunal committed a Shri Imran S/O Iqbaol Shaikh vs Shri Pappu S/O Saheblal Inmdar on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165727725/
2 grave error in assessing the disability and has awarded meager compensation on all heads.

entities.text: Imran S/O Iqbaol Shaikh vs Shri Pappu S/O Saheblal Inmdar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that the appellant sustained grievous injuries to his left leg and his left leg is amputed above knee.
Hence, he seeks to NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB re-assess the compensation keeping in mind the settled position of law by allowing the appeal.
5. Per contra, Sri. M.K.Soudagar, learned counsel, appearing for respondent No.2-insurance company opposes the appeal and seeks to sustain the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal.

He submits that the doctor, who has been examined as P.W.3 before the Tribunal, has assessed the disability at 80% and considering the same, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the same 40%, which does not call for any modification.

He further submits that the Tribunal taking note of the income-tax returns filed by the appellant has assessed the income of the injured claimant at Rs.25,000/- per month which also does not call for any modification.
He submits that the compensation awarded on other conventional heads is just and proper which needs no interference.

Thus, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.
6.
We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2- NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB insurance company.
Perused the material on record including the records of the Tribunal.
7. Pleadings and evidence on record indicate that on 09.10.2017, the appellant/claimant met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries.
Initially, he was taken to Civil Hospital at Miraj and thereafter he was shifted to Dr.Shaikh Hospital, Miraj.
The appellant/claimant's left leg has been amputed above knee after performing surgery.

It is averred that the appellant was aged about 30 years as on the date of the accident, he was an Engineer by profession and was earning Rs.50,000/-
per month.

It is further case of the appellant that, due to the accident, the appellant/claimant sustained permanent disability and he is unable to work and earn any income which he used to do prior to the accident.
It is also contended that the entire family was depending on the earnings of the injured claimant, and hence, claim petition was filed before the Tribunal.
The respondent-insurer opposed the claim petition before the Tribunal by filing objection.

In support of the NC:
2024:KHC-D:11554-DB claim petition, the injured examined himself as P.W.1 and two more witnesses as P.W.2 and P.W.3.
8.

Before adverting to disability of the appellant, it would be useful to refer to the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rajkumar Vs Ajay Kumar & Another1, wherein relevant paragraphs read thus:
"11. What requires to be assessed by the Tribunal is the effect of the permanently disability on the earning capacity of the injured; and after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of a percentage of the income, it has to be quantified in terns of money, to arrive at the future loss of earnings (by applying the standard multiplier method used to determine loss of dependency).

We may however note that in some cases, on appreciation of evidence and assessment, the Tribunal may find that percentage of loss of earning capacity as a result of the permanent disability, is approximately the same as the percentage of permanent disability in which case, of Shri Imran S/O Iqbaol Shaikh vs Shri Pappu S/O Saheblal Inmdar on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165727725/

entities.text: Shri Imran S/O Iqbaol Shaikh vs Shri Pappu S/O Saheblal Inmdar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 course, the Tribunal will adopt the said percentage for determination of compensation.
13. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The Tribunal has to first ascertain what activities the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of the permanent ability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood, or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying (2011) 1 SCC 343 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB on, or (iii) whether he was prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions, but could carry on some other or lesser scale of activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood.
14. For example, if the left hand of a claimant is amputated, the permanent physical or functional disablement may be assessed around 60%.
If the claimant was a driver or a carpenter, the actual loss of earning capacity may virtually be hundred percent, if he is neither able to drive or do carpentry.

On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less.

In fact, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of `loss of future earnings', if the claimant continues in government service, though he may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities as a consequence of losing his hand.

Sometimes the injured claimant may be continued in service, but may not found suitable for discharging the duties attached to the post or job which he was earlier holding, on account of his disability, and may therefore be shifted to some other suitable but lesser post with lesser emoluments, in which case there should be a limited award under the head of loss of future earning capacity, taking note of the reduced earning capacity."
(Emphasis supplied)

9. In another decision, the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Laxman Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited2, at paragraph-15 of the judgment has held as under:
(2011) 10 SCC 756 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB "15.

entities.text: Laxman Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The ration of the above noted judgments is that if the victim of an accident suffers permanent or temporary disability, then efforts should always be made to award adequate compensation not only for physical injury and treatment, but also for the pain, suffering and trauma caused due to the accident, loss of earnings and victim's inability to lead a normal life and enjoy amenities, which he would have enjoyed but for the disability caused due Shri Imran S/O Iqbaol Shaikh vs Shri Pappu S/O Saheblal Inmdar on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165727725/
4 to the accident."

entities.text: Imran S/O Iqbaol Shaikh vs Shri Pappu S/O Saheblal Inmdar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (emphasis supplied)

10. It is apt and necessary to refer the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Jagdish Vs.
Mohan & Others3, wherein at paragraph-14 is observed as under:
14.
In making the computation in the present case, the Court must be mindful of the fact that the appellant has suffered a serious disability in which he has suffered a loss of the use of both his hands.
For a person engage in manual activities, it requires no stretch of imagination to understand that a loss of hands is a complete deprivation of the ability to earn.
Nothing- atleast in the facts of this case- can restore lost hands.
But the measure of compensation must reflect a genuine attempt of the law to restore the dignity of the being.
Our yardsticks of compensation should not be so abysmal as to lead one to question whether our law values human life.
If it does, as it must, it must provide a realistic recompense for the pain of loss and the trauma of suffering.
Awards of compensation are not law's doles.
In a discourse of rights, they constitute entitlements under law.
Our conversations about law must shift from a paternalistic subordination of the individual to an assertion of enforceable rights as intrinsic to human dignity.
(Emphasis supplied) (2018) 4 SCC 571 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB 11.

In a recent decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of SARNAM SINGH Vs. SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND ORTHERS4, has held as under:
"9.

entities.text: SARNAM SINGH Vs. SHRIRAM GENERAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND ORTHERS4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As to how compensation, in case where permanent disability of an injured affects his functional disability, is to be assessed has been considered by this Court,
repeatedly.

Reference can be made to the judgment of this Court in Mohan Soni vs.
Ram Avtar Tomar And Others.

entities.text:
Mohan Soni vs.
Ram Avtar Tomar And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the aforesaid case the injured was working as a cart puller.
As a result of the accident, his left leg was amputated.
His permanent disability was assessed at 60%.
The Tribunal assessed the compensation taking the loss of earning at 50% on the theory that he can still do some other work while sitting.
The High Court did not disturb the finding regarding loss of income on account of disability.
This Court found that the Tribunal was in error in taking the loss of earning at 50% as the injured was 55 years of age and it may be difficult for him to find a job at that stage.
In fact, any physical disability resulting from an accident has to be judged with reference to the nature of the work being performed by the person who suffered disability.
The same injury suffered by two different persons may affect them in different ways.
Loss of leg by a farmer or a rickshaw puller may be end of the road as far as his earning capacity is concerned.
Whereas, in case of the persons engaged in some kind of desk work in office, loss of leg may have lesser effect.
This Court enhanced the loss of earning capacity from 50% to 90%."
(Emphasis supplied)
2023 LiveLaw (SC) 498

Shri Imran S/O Iqbaol Shaikh vs Shri Pappu S/O Saheblal Inmdar on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165727725/
5 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB 12.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sidram Vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited & Another5, at paragraph-31 has held as under:
"31.

entities.text: Sidram Vs. Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Company Limited & Another5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is now a well settled position of law that even in cases of permanent disablement incurred as a result of a motor-accident, the claimant can seek, apart from compensation for future loss of income, amounts for future prospects as well.

We have come across many orders of different tribunals and unfortunately affirmed by different High Courts, taking the view that the claimant is not entitled to compensation for future prospects in accident cases involving serious injuries resulting in permanent disablement.
That is not a correct position of law.
There is no justification to exclude the possibility of compensation for future prospects in accident cases involving serious injuries resulting in permanent disablement.

Such a narrow reading is illogical because it denies altogether the possibility of the living victim progressing further in life in accident cases - and admits such possibility of future prospects, in case of the victim's death."
(Emphasis supplied) (2023) 3 SCC 439 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB 13.

Keeping in mind the enunciation of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court referred supra,
now the case on hand is dealt with on the basis of available evidence.
The oral testimony of P.W.3 indicates that the appellant/claimant's left leg was amputed due to accidental injuries.
It is opined by the doctor that the appellant/claimant has sustained disability to an extent of 80%.

Taking note of the oral testimony of P.W.3 and Schedule to Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, we are of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to re-assess the disability suffered by the injured claimant/appellant at 80% as he would be unable to work as he used to work prior to the accident.

The appellant due to the accident lost his future happiness, hope and expectation of life,
and also he will not be able to enjoy the marital life.
The normal expectation of life of the appellant is also impaired.

The mental and physical loss of the injured cannot be reckoned in terms of money,
but there is no other way to compensate the victim except by payment of just compensation.

No amount of compensation can restore - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB the physical frame of the appellant and also it is impossible to equate the money with the human sufferings or personal deprivations.

Hence, taking note of all these aspects into consideration, this Court is of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate Shri Imran S/O Iqbaol Shaikh vs Shri Pappu S/O Saheblal Inmdar on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165727725/
6

entities.text: Iqbaol Shaikh vs Shri Pappu S/O Saheblal Inmdar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: to assess the functional disability of the appellant at 80%, which would meet the ends of justice.
14. The Tribunal considering Ex.P.37 to 43 - Income- tax Returns filed by the injured claimant/appellant has assessed the income of the injured claimant/appellant at Rs.25,000/- per month.

Perusal of those documents on record indicates that the claimant/appellant was getting Rs.15,000/- per month for the years 2007-10, which increased to Rs.30,000/- per month for the years 2010-13, and further increased to Rs.35,000/- for the years 2013-14.
In the instant case, the accident has taken place 09.10.2017.

Considering the growth of income from 2013 to 2017, and his educational qualification and professional competency, we are of the considered view that it would be - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB just and appropriate to re-assess the income of the appellant/claimant at Rs.30,000/- per month.
15.

Having assessed the income of the appellant/claimant at Rs.30,000/- per month and the disability at 80%, and on applying the appropriate multiplier '17' having regard to the age of claimant as 30 years, the appellant/claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.48,96,000/-
[Rs.30,000 x 80% x 12 x 17].
16. The appellant/claimant was aged 30 years as on the date of the accident and is entitled to an addition of 40% of the assessed income towards 'loss of future prospects'.
Hence, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.19,58,400/- [40% of Rs.48,96,000/-] under the said head.
17. The evidence on record indicates that the appellant has taken treatment in two hospitals i.e., in Civil Hospital, Miraj, and thereafter in Dr.Shaikh Hospital, Miraj, and underwent a surgery.

Hence,
considering the same, it - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB would be just and appropriate to award a sum of Rs.1,20,000/- under the head 'loss of income during treatment period' considering the income at Rs.30,000/- per month and the period of treatment as four months.
18. Insofar as the contention of the appellant that the appellant lost marriage prospects due to disability/amputation, the same requires consideration.
Admittedly, the appellant is a bachelor, and was aged about 30 years at the time of the accident.
Taking note of the same we award a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- under head loss of marriage prospects.

19. Insofar as awarding of compensation under the heads 'pain and suffering', 'medical expenses',
'conveyance, attendant, nourishment', and 'loss of amenities the same is remains unaltered.

20. On re-assessment, the claimant is entitled to a total compensation as under:
Shri Imran S/O Iqbaol Shaikh vs Shri Pappu S/O Saheblal Inmdar on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165727725/
7
1. Towards pain & sufferings Rs. 30,000/-

2. Towards medical expenses Rs. 1,01,693/-
- 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB 3. Towards conveyance, attendant, Rs. 30,000/-
nourishment 4. Loss of amenities and future Rs. 1,00,000/-
unhappiness 5. Loss of income during laid up Rs. 1,20,000 period 6. Loss of future income Rs. 48,96,000/-
7.
Towards Loss of future prospects Rs. 19,58,400/-
8. Towards loss of marriage prospects Rs. 2,00,000/-
Thus, the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.74,36,093/- as against Rs.31,57,693/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The enhanced compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

21. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2-insurance company submits appellant/claimant may be held not entitled to interest on the amount of Rs.19,58,400/- awarded towards 'loss of future prospects'.
Learned counsel for the appellant also fairly submits that the appellant may be held not entitled to interest on the amount awarded under the head 'loss of future prospects'.

In view of the decision of a Coordinate Bench of this Court in Chandrakala and another vs. Dilipkumar & Another6, it M.F.A. No.1662/2023, disposed of on 02.07.2024 - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB is made clear that the appellant/claimant is not entitled to interest on the amount awarded under the head 'loss of future prospects.

8 22.

In the result, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to an extent that the claimant is entitled to total compensation Rs.74,36,093/- as against Rs.31,57,693/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of payment.
d) As observed above, the amount of Rs.19,58,400/-, being 40% of the assessed income awarded towards 'loss of future prospects' shall not carry any interest.

- 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:11554-DB e) The Respondent No.2-insurance company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from today.
f) The apportionment, deposit and  disbursement of enhanced compensation shall be made as per award of the Tribunal.
Draw modified award accordingly.
